claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a relatively coarse dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The dual-phase microstructure can consist of a ductile FCC phase interwoven with a strengthening BCC phase.
A brief post-solidification anneal at a temperature slightly below the eutectic temperature will refine the lamellar spacing.
Refining the lamellar spacing through this anneal will simultaneously increase strength and ductility.
The anneal should be applied immediately after solidification.
Applying the treatment immediately after casting will prevent unwanted coarsening.
Controlled annealing promotes precipitation in the strengthening phase.
The annealing treatment preserves a continuous, deformable ductile-phase network.
The resulting microstructure reduces the effective dislocation slip length.
Precipitation and interface strengthening increase strength.
The treated microstructure mitigates dislocation pile-ups and premature crack nucleation.
Mitigating pile-ups and premature crack nucleation produces more uniform deformation and greater ductility.
The treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The treatment will increase ductility by approximately 30% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The simultaneous improvements should hold during standard tensile testing at ambient or moderately elevated temperatures.
Departures from the required annealing temperature or duration, including over-annealing, may negate or reverse the benefits.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis identifies lamellar refinement as the mediator, while the mechanism says that the same anneal promotes coarsening. Refinement and coarsening are opposing structural changes, and their respective roles are not reconciled.
